lines.trans: Hey, Vanya, get up, get up!
Come on, get up, you'll freeze in the snow!
Arise, vast country...
What country? Get on your feet!
A vast country...
You slept here all night!
Where am I? What time is it?
It's already morning, people are walking past.
Lyokha! Where is my friend Lyokha?
Your friend is sleeping at home.
Listen, do you need a tank?
Go and take it!

meanings.note: The neuter form 'всё' used alone. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Neuter всё. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Plural все. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.

вставать.gloss: to get up, to stand up

meanings.note: Out of bed or from the floor. Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'тавать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to get up, to stand up', paired with 'встать'.
Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'тавать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to get up, to stand up', paired with 'встать'.

examples.trans: Come on, Tuzik, let's get up!
I get up at seven in the morning.
Come on, Tuzik, let's get up!

meanings.note: Location; for direction use 'куда'. Core Russian adv meaning 'where' in everyday speech.

examples.text: А где машинка? Где моя машинка?
examples.trans: Hey, where's the toy car? Where's my toy car?

meanings.note: давай + 1st person plural or infinitive
давай + 1st person plural or infinitive

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.
examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.

meanings.note: Location; compare домой = homeward. Core Russian adv meaning 'at home' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: The main thing is, you keep him at home.

examples.text: А Осипенко сейчас дома лежит. У него больное сердце.
examples.trans: And Osipenko is lying at home right now. He has a sick heart.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'friend' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: This is Vanya, my childhood friend.

examples.text: Это Паша, мой заместитель. Это Ваня, друг моего детства.
examples.trans: This is Pasha, my deputy. This is Vanya, my childhood friend.

meanings.note: забирать деньги = to take the money
забирать детей из школы = to pick the kids up from school

examples.trans: I pick the children up from school.

examples.text: А я тебе делаю условный срок. Плюс ты забираешь все деньги Вики.
examples.trans: And I get you a suspended sentence. Plus you take all of Vika's money.

meanings.en: to get cold, feel chilled; to freeze solid
meanings.note: intransitive; past tense замёрз, замёрзла

examples.trans: Danya, are you cold or what?
Come on, get up, you'll freeze in the snow!

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: In one direction, now. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to go (on foot)', paired with 'пойти'.
To run for a second term. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to go (on foot)', paired with 'пойти'.

examples.trans: He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: In questions. Core Russian det meaning 'what; what a' in everyday speech.
in exclamations: какой грязный! = how dirty!

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: joins a description to a noun; agrees with that noun in gender and number

examples.trans: This is a mayor who keeps his word.
Where is the book that was here?

examples.text: А что я за мэр такой, который держит своё слово?
examples.trans: And what kind of mayor would I be if I kept my word?

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: It's already morning, people are walking past.

meanings.note: Agrees with the thing owned. Core Russian det meaning 'my, mine' in everyday speech.
+ prepositional: на сайте. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.
+ accusative: на второй срок. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Russian uses one word for both. Common feminine noun meaning 'leg, foot' in everyday Russian.
Russian uses one word for both. Common feminine noun meaning 'leg, foot' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Заходите. Поставьте, пожалуйста, правую ногу на кровать.
examples.trans: Come in. Please put your right foot on the bed.

meanings.note: ночью = at night; спокойной ночи = good night

examples.text: Ну что, Аркаша? Наступила ночь, просыпается мафия.
examples.trans: So, Arkasha? Night has fallen, the mafia wakes up.

meanings.note: short form 'нужен / нужна / нужно / нужны' + dative: 'мне нужна работа' = I need a job
Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('huge, enormous').

examples.text: Кстати, если хочешь, иди к нам в команду. Шансы у нас огромные.
examples.trans: By the way, if you want, join our team. Our chances are huge.

meanings.note: accusative/genitive его (него after prepositions), dative ему (нему)
For masculine and neuter things. Core Russian pron meaning 'he; it' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: его (gen/acc), ему (dat), им (instr), нём (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'he; it' in everyday speech.

проспать.gloss: to sleep through, overslept; sleep for

meanings.en: to sleep for (a duration of time); to oversleep
meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'спать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to sleep through, overslept; sleep for', paired with 'просыпать'.

examples.trans: Boss, excuse me, I simply overslept.

meanings.note: Слышать о + prepositional. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лышать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to hear', paired with 'услышать'.

Слышать о + prepositional. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лышать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to hear', paired with 'услышать'.

examples.text: Как странно, я ничего об этом не слышал.
examples.trans: How strange, I've heard nothing about it.

meanings.note: Locative в снегу after в/на. Common masculine noun meaning 'snow' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Right now we will clear the snow.
White snow lies in the forest.

examples.text: Ой, тут кругом снег! А где мы сидеть будем?
examples.trans: Oh, there is snow all around here! And where are we going to sit?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'пать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to sleep', paired with 'поспать'.

examples.text: Ладно, утром позвоню ей. Поехали спать.
examples.trans: All right, I'll call her in the morning. Let's go to sleep.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'трана'). Common feminine noun meaning 'country' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The whole country is laughing at you!

examples.text: Над тобой вся страна смеётся! Все видели, как ты из окна летел.
examples.trans: The whole country is laughing at you! Everyone saw you fly out the window.

meanings.note: military armored combat vehicle or toy replica

examples.text: Вы очень долго чините мой танк.
examples.trans: You are taking very long to fix my tank.

meanings.note: To someone you call ты. Core Russian det meaning 'your (informal)' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.

meanings.note: Colloquial, like здесь. Core Russian adv meaning 'here' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: There's someone here to see you.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

meanings.note: One person, informal. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: уже четыре года = for four years now

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been mayor for four years now.

meanings.note: Утром = in the morning. Common neuter noun meaning 'morning' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Какое хорошее утро! Лидия Алексеевна, чашку кофе, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: What a lovely morning! Lidia Alekseyevna, a cup of coffee, please.

meanings.note: В два часа = at two o'clock. Common masculine noun meaning 'hour' in everyday Russian.
В два часа = at two o'clock. Common masculine noun meaning 'hour' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I'll be there in an hour.

examples.text: Слушай, я уеду на полтора часа. Ты с Викой посиди, понял?
examples.trans: Listen, I'm going out for an hour and a half. You stay with Vika, got it?

час.governs: after 2, 3, 4 and полтора the genitive часа is stressed on the ending

meanings.note: the plural is a different word: люди, людям, о людях
Plural люди, a different word. Common masculine noun meaning 'person; (pl) people' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: There are a lot of people here.
I know the problems of ordinary people.

meanings.note: To get someone's attention. Core Russian interj meaning 'hey' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Хорошая, никто же не говорит. Эй, ты что?
examples.trans: She is good, nobody's saying she isn't. Hey, what's wrong?

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'I' in everyday speech.
